fact: 1924年12月1日，普鲁塔科·埃利亚斯·卡列斯（Plutarco Elías Calles）就任墨西哥总统，这是自1884年以来墨西哥首次和平的总统权力交接。卡列斯此前在奥布雷贡政府中任内政部长（1920—1923），1923年奥布雷贡支持他竞选总统，引发前财政部长德拉韦尔塔的叛乱（1923年底），叛乱被迅速平定。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Plutarco Elías Calles
sources.quote: Calles then easily won the presidential election and assumed office on December 1, 1924, the first peaceful transfer of power in Mexico since 1884.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Álvaro Obregón's Vision for Mexico
sources.quote: When his term was over, Obregón left power and returned to Sonora, the first peaceful transition of the presidency since Porfirio Díaz was overthrown 14 years before. The Mexican Revolution was finally over.

fact: 卡列斯就任后推行大规模现代化计划：创建墨西哥银行（Banco de México）稳定金融体系、开征所得税、建设铁路公路桥梁水坝、派遣教师到农村开展公共卫生和疫苗接种运动、建立农业学校改善耕作技术。土地改革继续推进：向1500个村社（ejido）分配了800万英亩土地。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Plutarco Elías Calles
sources.quote: He secured Mexico's finances by creating the Bank of Mexico, and he initiated Mexico's first income tax. He instituted a massive public works program to build Mexico's infrastructure: railroads, roads, bridges, dams, canals, and air service. ... In land reform, he distributed eight million acres to fifteen hundred ejidos.

sources.title: 中国社会科学院拉丁美洲研究所，卡耶斯
sources.quote: 1924—1928年任总统期间,进行了土地改革,在1576个村庄分配了320多万公顷土地;成立水利和道路委员会,建筑一批水坝和公路;建立了农业信贷银行、墨西哥银行等。

fact: 卡列斯通过与劳工领袖路易斯·莫罗内斯（Luis Morones，CROM工会联盟主席）的关系控制劳工运动，压制罢工但适度提高工资和福利。莫罗内斯被任命为劳工部长，利用职权把所有不驯服的劳工团体纳入控制。CROM（墨西哥区域工人联合会）是奥布雷贡和卡列斯时期政府支持的主要工会组织。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Plutarco Elías Calles
sources.quote: His cabinet was filled with cronies who became wealthy by looting the treasury. The most notorious of these so-called forty thieves was Luis Morones, head of the Confederacion Regional Obrera Mexicana (CROM), whom Calles made secretary of labor. Morones used his position to bring all recalcitrant labor groups under his control. ... Calles used his relationship with Morones to keep labor strikes down while modestly increasing wages and other benefits.

sources.title: Britannica, Mexico: The Mexican Revolution and its aftermath
sources.quote: The government supported the Regional Confederation of Mexican Labour (Confederación Regional de Obreros Mexicanos; CROM).

fact: 卡列斯创建了墨西哥银行（Banco de México），开征墨西哥第一项所得税，稳定了国家金融体系。1920年代墨西哥经济处于扩张期，有收入来源支撑现代化计划。奥布雷贡时期墨西哥货币回归金本位，邀请外国公司投资基础设施，石油出口从1919年的7770万桶增加到1921年的1.9亿桶。1923年布卡雷利协议（Bucareli Agreements）使美墨关系正常化。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Plutarco Elías Calles
sources.quote: He secured Mexico's finances by creating the Bank of Mexico, and he initiated Mexico's first income tax. ... He had come to power at a moment when the Mexican economy was expanding and there were revenues available to finance his modernization program.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Álvaro Obregón's Vision for Mexico
sources.quote: Obregón returned Mexican currency to the gold standard and invited foreign visitors and companies to invest in Mexico's infrastructure, revitalized Mexico's economy and increasing Mexican oil exported abroad. Under de la Huerta and Obregón after him, oil exports rose from 77,703,289 barrels in 1919 to 190,000,000 by the end of 1921. The Obregón government signed the Bucareli Agreements with the U.S. in 1923, normalizing relations between the two nations.

fact: 1917年墨西哥宪法第27条确立了地下资源（矿物、石油等）归国家所有，限制了外国公司的特权。1925年卡列斯要求所有国内外石油公司将其产权换成50年租约，美墨关系因此紧张。1927年美国大使莫罗抵达墨西哥城后达成妥协：1927年墨西哥最高法院裁定石油公司必须遵守法律，但租约在50年后不会被终止。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Plutarco Elías Calles
sources.quote: Calles also zealously enforced the constitution's provisions regarding state control over natural resources. In 1925, Calles ordered all domestic and foreign oil companies to exchange their titles for fifty-year leases. Consequently, United States-Mexican relations became strained. In 1927, Ambassador Dwight M. Morrow arrived in Mexico City to resolve the crisis. ... In 1927, the Mexican Supreme Court ruled that the oil companies had to comply with the law, but the leases would not be terminated in fifty years.

sources.title: Historia Mundum, Mexican Revolution
sources.quote: State ownership of subsoil resources: It was declared that all minerals, oil, and other riches of the Mexican subsoil would belong to the Mexican State. This curbed the privileges of foreign companies and laid the groundwork for national exploitation of these strategic resources.

fact: 1917年墨西哥宪法是革命的制度性成果：确立地下资源国有化、土地改革（ejido制度）、劳工权利入宪（最低工资、限制童工和女工、工会合法化、罢工权）。这些理想在奥布雷贡和卡列斯时期逐步实施但进展缓慢。1926年卡列斯法（Calles Law）将天主教会置于国家控制之下，关闭教会学校、驱逐外国神父，引发1926—1929年的基督战争（Cristero War）。

sources.title: Historia Mundum, Mexican Revolution
sources.quote: Labor rights entered constitutional law: For the first time in Mexican history, labor guarantees were included in a constitution. For example, minimum wage, limits on child and female labor, legalization of unions, and the right to strike. ... One of Calles's most controversial acts was the promulgation of the so-called Calles Law in 1926. It subordinated the Catholic Church to state control and severely restricted freedom of worship.

sources.title: Britannica, Mexico: The Mexican Revolution and its aftermath
sources.quote: Problems with the church developed when Calles instituted vigorously anticlerical measures; in retaliation the church suspended all religious ceremonies and approved and possibly sponsored a rebellion in western Mexico known as the Cristeros.

fact: 卡列斯时期大规模公共工程建设启动：铁路、公路、桥梁、水坝、运河和航空服务。农业银行建立提供信贷（但大部分贷款流向卡列斯派和大庄园主，成为腐败来源）。公共卫生和疫苗接种运动、农业学校改善耕作技术。公路建设委员会和水利委员会成立。墨西哥的基础设施在1920年代逐步现代化。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Plutarco Elías Calles
sources.quote: He instituted a massive public works program to build Mexico's infrastructure: railroads, roads, bridges, dams, canals, and air service. He sent teachers into isolated rural areas, and he began national public health and inoculation campaigns. Agricultural schools were established to improve farming techniques. ... Agricultural banks were established to provide credit, but this proved to be a major source of corruption as most of the loans went to Callistas and hacendados.

sources.title: 中国社会科学院拉丁美洲研究所，卡耶斯
sources.quote: 成立水利和道路委员会,建筑一批水坝和公路;建立了农业信贷银行、墨西哥银行等。

fact: 1920年代墨西哥经济扩张期，城市就业和收入有所改善，但农村地区依然贫困。卡列斯的农业信贷银行大部分贷款流向政治盟友和大庄园主，普通农民获得信贷困难。土地改革分配了800万英亩土地给1500个村社，但大庄园（如特拉萨斯的250万英亩庄园）依然存在。城市生活成本在现代化计划推进中逐步上升。

sources.title: Library of Congress, Álvaro Obregón's Vision for Mexico
sources.quote: During his presidency, Obregón gave 3,250,000 acres of land back to 400,000 citizens, but large estates, such as Luis Terrazas' 2.5 million acre property, continued as before.

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Plutarco Elías Calles
sources.quote: Agricultural banks were established to provide credit, but this proved to be a major source of corruption as most of the loans went to Callistas and hacendados.
